extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus
extraction.description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. It contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar). The ACL OCL spans seven decades, containing 73,285 papers published from 1952 to September 2022, alongside 210K figures.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.publisher: Pennsylvania State University; National University of Singapore
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual (96 languages, predominantly English; including Latin, Gujarati, etc.)
extraction.citeAs: Rohatgi, S., Qin, Y., Aw, B., Unnithan, N., & Kan, M.-Y. (2023). The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Authors designed crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. PDF files longer than 50 pages (mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks) were removed. Full texts were extracted from PDFs using GROBID, and figures/tables extracted using PDFFigures. The corpus was linked to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) via its Graph API to enrich with external information such as citations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Certain fields are only valid on a portion of the papers. For example, only 16.8% of OCL papers have arxiv_paper_id, indicating a corresponding version in arXiv.org. Full-text extraction fails mostly for papers between 2000 to 2015.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF files and metadata crawled from the ACL Anthology website (https://aclanthology.org/), supplemented with data from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) via its Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Metadata from the ACL Anthology website is used in place of metadata extracted from PDFs, given the website's author-driven nature yields more accurate metadata. Citation network constructed using in-degree (internal citations) and citations (external citations via S2AG Graph Paper Lookup API).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Full texts were extracted from PDFs using GROBID and formatted in S2ORC-JSON schema. Figures and tables were extracted using PDFFigures. Language was detected using a public language detection toolkit with title and abstract as inputs. Papers were linked to S2AG using ACL Anthology ID.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the topic classification subset (STop), papers from conferences (ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, NAACL 2021) were crawled along with their author-submitted topic labels from the conference websites. For the full OCL corpus, silver topic labels were generated by a trained PLM-based (SPECTER) classification model. Language labels were automatically detected using a language detection toolkit.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors manually checked 21 documents to assess the quality of full texts (metadata, general texts, and specialized formats). Quality issues identified include incorrect author names, missing section names, merged paragraphs, mixed footnotes, and misidentified table captions. 19 sections were not detected from 21 papers; 28.78% of figures and 31.58% of tables were not detected.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One topic label per paper (single-label classification setting).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID (full-text extraction), PDFFigures 2.0 (figure/table extraction), langdetect (language detection toolkit by Nakatani Shuyo), BART-large-MNLI, SciBERT, SPECTER (for topic classification).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which new papers added to the ACL Anthology are downloaded and processed. New additions are identified by monitoring changes in URLs. The authors plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive. The ultimate goal is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Author names and affiliations are included as part of the metadata of scientific papers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus facilitates open scientific research in computational linguistics, supports reproducibility, enables topic trend analysis highlighting emerging topics like Ethics of NLP and declining underrepresented topics like Discourse and Pragmatics, and enables analysis of language representation in the field.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is biased toward English-language papers, with English being the most dominant language. Low-resource languages remain underrepresented, with significant disparity in coverage even among languages in the same language group. The distribution of top-cited papers is biased toward dominant topics such as Machine Translation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCL is a small-scale collection focused on peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology only; it does not include other sources. Full-text extraction quality is limited by GROBID's inherent limitations (issues with metadata such as author names, missing section names, merged paragraphs, footnotes mixed with text, misidentified table captions, in-line equations, figures, and tables). Only open-source toolkits were considered due to budget constraints. The corpus is unlabeled, lacking annotations for specific tasks. Full-text extraction fails mostly for papers between 2000 to 2015.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Use cases include: topic analysis and trend detection, emerging topic detection, paper-reviewer matching, document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training/fine-tuning scientific LLMs, summarization, related work generation, information extraction from specific sections (e.g., contribution extraction, future work prediction), multimodal research tasks (figure caption generation), historical language change analysis, and knowledge graph construction. The dataset was used for training, validation, and testing of topic classification models (5-fold cross-validation with 2036 training and 509 test papers).
